title: Trump calls on New Mexico to change its name to ‘New America’ | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

President Donald Trump on Monday called on New Mexico to change its name to “New America” — the latest example of him seeking geographical name changes that fit his political agenda.

“New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America. We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America!” Trump wrote onTruth Social, shortly before departing the White House for a midterm rally in Kansas.

His comments about New Mexico — a blue state he lost by 6 points in 2024 — come as Republicans are anxious about holding their congressional majorities in November, with voters saying in polling that the president isn’t paying enough attention to the country’s most pressing problems.

Trump claimed, without citing any evidence, that “home values and incomes would rise” because of a name change. And he repeated his baseless claims about rigged elections by adding, “Maybe even the Crooked Elections, that New Mexico is known for, would become honest again!”

Trump has previously suggested renaming New Mexico, although not so forcefully. In September, heposted to social mediaa map of the state with the word “Mexico” crossed out and “America” written underneath — an image that wasrepostedby the White House X account.

It’s just the latest renaming push from Trump. He signed an executive order in August tochange the name of Lake Ontario to “Lake America”as part of his ongoing trade war with Canada. He took similar action last year to rename the Gulf of Mexico to “Gulf of America.” The president has also repeatedly floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz the “Trump Strait.”

But while Trump has the power to rename what geographic landmarks, such as bodies of water, are called in the Geographic Names Information System, he doesn’t have the constitutional ability to legally rename states. That process would need to happen within the state.

New Mexico’s name predates the founding of the United States back to the 16th century, according toa fact sheet on the originof state names from the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

New Mexico Democratic Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham on Monday evening dismissed Trump’s comments.

“Let me repeat: New Mexico was New Mexico long before the United States existed and we’ll be New Mexico forevermore,” she wrote in apost on X.

Sen. Ben Ray Luján of New Mexico wrote in asocial postthat the state’s name “carries generations of history, culture, and rich traditions that continue to shape who we are.”

“We are New Mexicans. We’re proud of our name, proud of our home, and we’re keeping both. Long after Donald Trump is out of office, we’ll still be New Mexico,” he continued.

This story has been updated with additional details.CNN’s Piper Hudspeth Blackburn contributed to this report.
